gate_pin_check.question: Is nd-unfolding/pet/step1_increment_trajectory.py in the Gate-4 code gate's pin list?
gate_pin_check.answer: NO. The PLAN's claim at :158-160 is CORRECT as stated.
derivation: Parsed the receipt and walked EVERY leaf, not just the `files` block: 138 string leaves total.
`files` is a dict of 19 entries resolving to 19 DISTINCT paths (19 == 19, no duplicates hiding a 20th).
Zero of the 138 string leaves contain the substring 'step1_increment_trajectory'.

Aliasing ruled out on the raw bytes rather than the parsed tree: 'trajectory' and 'step1' both DO occur in the file (so a null result is not an artifact of a failed search), while 'increment' occurs zero times.

transitive_freeze_discovered.summary: The Gate-4 answer is right and INSUFFICIENT. The PLAN says the change costs 'only a new launcher pin, because the trajectory launcher hardcodes its sha256'. Derived: THREE launchers hardcode it, and TWO of those three are themselves frozen by active run receipts, so an in-place re-pin is not available.
transitive_freeze_discovered.how_it_was_caught: The in-place re-pin was made in all three, then `docs/orchestration/verify_hash_bindings.py` returned rc=1 with two MISMATCHes and `nd-unfolding/tests/test_hash_bindings.py::test_no_new_broken_hash_bindings` went red. It was NOT caught by reading; it was caught by running the verifier after the write.
transitive_freeze_discovered.why_the_edit_was_reverted_rather_than_th: verify_hash_bindings.py's own docstring: 'A stale pin is not repaired by editing the hash. The constant records what the gate ran against... Re-issue the owning gate and record the move.' Both receipts are submit-time provenance of runs that COMPLETED (56847059 and 56863958). Rewriting their hashes to accommodate a later code change would falsify what ran. Appending them to KNOWN_PREEXISTING was also rejected: that set is explicitly scoped to drift 'before 2026-07-28' and laundering new drift through it defeats the instrument.
transitive_freeze_discovered.resolution_taken: No existing launcher is touched. All three keep pinning 48f8353d, which stays CORRECT because they read the code out of /pscratch/sd/j/josephrb/gate6-reconcile-56834281 and that tree is left byte-identical (verified there: 48f8353d, same turn). The new pin lives in a NEW launcher that runs from its own checkout.
transitive_freeze_discovered.residual_hazard_not_fixed_by_this_lane: Syncing the flag-carrying step1_increment_trajectory.py into gate6-reconcile-56834281 would break the trajectory, floor-replicate and legx launchers simultaneously with 'code hash mismatch'. Leg 0 avoids this by construction (G6_LEG0_CODE_REPO is mandatory and the frozen trees are refused), but the hazard remains for anyone else who syncs. Filed as BEN-201.

semantics.auto: prefer OmniFold_<name>_iter<i>_step<s>_final.weights.h5, fall back to the best-epoch file, die if neither exists. Byte-for-byte the pre-flag rule.
semantics.best-epoch: force the best-epoch file for EVERY iteration and step; die if absent, never fall back.
semantics.final: force the _final file for EVERY iteration and step; die if absent, never fall back. On the eight-checkpoint member inventory this cannot be satisfied at iterations 0 and 1, by design -- the mode exists so the auto fallback is not the only way to ask for _final.

code_change.why_no_fallback_on_an_explicit_tier: A silent downgrade would hand back the other tier's weights while the receipt recorded the requested one, so a best-vs-final contrast would compare a tier against itself and measure a gap of ZERO -- reading as 'no tier artifact', which is the exact conclusion this leg exists to test.
other_changes_all_additive: resolve_checkpoint() lifted from a closure inside main() to module level, so the control is testable without the TensorFlow stack main() imports. No behaviour change; main()'s ckpt() now delegates.
trajectory rows gain checkpoint_tier_step2. push_dev_vs_R -- and therefore the Gate-6 metric -- is a STEP-2 quantity, and only the step-1 tier was being reported.

the GATE_FAILED payload gains R, niter, checkpoint_tier_requested, checkpoints, repro_rtol, gate_is_cross_tier and the two input paths, so |push_final/R - 1| stays derivable from a failed run instead of the run being lost (CONVENTION-receipt-ingredients, BEN-077).
payload gains checkpoint_tier_requested; the caveat string is tier-conditional so a tier-clean run does not carry the mixed-tier caveat.
not_changed: REPRO_RTOL stays 0.02 in every mode. It was deliberately NOT relaxed for the cross-tier case: a threshold that means something different per mode is not a threshold.
the reproduction gate still fails closed in every mode.
